per_subject_auc_known_issue.bug: The per_subject_auc field in each claim below was computed by a trapezoidal integration over roc_estimability.threshold_derivation.build_roc_points()'s output, which deliberately has no candidate threshold ABOVE the maximum observed score (theta1/theta2 derivation never needs one). This means the reported AUC never includes the final ROC segment out to FPR=1.0 -- for a claim whose honest distribution is a single repeated ceiling value (Device/Model/FSI's deterministic pass/fail claims), this silently capped every subject's reported AUC toward 0.0 even though separation is perfect (confirmed independently: theta1==theta2==100, band_cap=HIGH for all three, and the spine_sanity_check rows above show clean Safe/Constrained classification for both honest and attack cases).
per_subject_auc_known_issue.fix: experiments/phase9_measured_roc.py's _per_subject_auc() now appends the standard ROC-closing corner (FPR=1.0, TPR=1.0) before integrating, fixed after this run completed. Per instruction, the experiment was NOT rerun to regenerate corrected numbers; this note documents the known-correct values (analytically derivable from the already-confirmed theta1/theta2 findings above) in place of a full rerun.
per_subject_auc_known_issue.scope_of_impact: This bug affects ONLY the per_subject_auc reporting field, which CLAUDE.md 14 states is reported as a distribution with no success criterion and is never used to derive theta1/theta2/resolution_status or to steer alpha/beta. It does NOT affect: theta1/theta2/band_cap (derived via trust_kernel.bands.derive_thresholds directly on the same roc_points, whose formula never needed an upper sentinel), resolution_status/Tail-Floor Rule evaluation (driven by class separation/bootstrap width/LOSO swing, none of which use this AUC computation), config/eis.v1-measured.json's content or hash, or the spine sanity check (which independently exercises the real trust_kernel pipeline against the derived thresholds and shows correct classification).
